substeps.label: Day 1
substeps.caption: The lab as set up: two Shuttles with every tray loaded and powered, the floor machines, two MiR250 + UR10e units on charge. The clock starts on a Monday at 06:00.

substeps.label: 1/4  Hour by hour
substeps.caption: Hour by hour, the first day. One person comes in 08:00-16:00: the atomizer's crucible first, then the day's upkeep where it is done (a tray held at a Shuttle's opening with the units kept away, a floor machine, a unit on its charger). The arms run their reference checks between jobs, and keep going with the lights off.

substeps.label: 2/4  Day by day
substeps.caption: Day by day. The atomizer runs only while someone is on site: one run a day while the lab is commissioned, then three a weekday. A beacon is amber while its machine is out for upkeep, red while a fault waits for the next shift or for parts; the rest runs round the clock.

substeps.label: 3/4  Week by week
substeps.caption: Week by week. Upkeep takes 18 of the person's 40 hours a week on average, the crucible 13 more. An alloy is fully tested about half a day after it is atomized; one in ten is promoted to a full plate of E8 bars.

substeps.label: 4/4  Month by month
substeps.caption: Month by month, to the end of the first year. Upkeep and failures cost 20 of the 324 alloys the same schedule would test with none (the faint line). A model built from each chapter's step times and the assumptions in notes/timelapse.md and notes/upkeep.md, not measurements.
